Enhancing People’s Lives for Over 50 Years.

## Discover Your Perfect Pairing

It’s easy to pair to impress! Our **Mushroom ****Small Bites & Beer Pairings Guide** features
pairings from our resident mushroom grower and craft brewer. Download your copy today and serve
culinary masterpiece pairings from the comfort of your own kitchen!

## Monterey Mushrooms Hosts an Award Ceremony to Congratulate Teammates’ Children Who Received
## Scholarships 

We proudly presented 81 children of its teammates with $237,300 in scholarship awards for the
2023-24 academic year. On August 10th, 2023, Shah Kazemi, CEO, presented 10 of those recipients with
their awards in person at the company's corporate office in Watsonville, California.

* [ [wild mushroom called boletus] ][198]
  
  [ wild mushroom called boletus ][199]
  
  By June 14, 2023
  
  Recently, a wild mushroom called boletus has attracted widespread attention in the market.
  According to experts, boletus is a high-protein, low-fat, nutritious edible fungus, and is known
  as the "king of fungi". Boletus grows in alpine forests above 1,500 meters above sea level, and
  the picking season is generally in autumn. Due to the difficulty in collecting, the price of
  boletus has remained high. However, with people's emphasis on healthy eating and their love for
  wild ingredients, porcini mushrooms have gradually become the darling of high-end restaurants and

# AUSTIN: Orchid Mycology Walk

Join us for a guided nature walk to observe the **Glass Mountain Crested Coralroot** (*Bletia
nitida*)—a threatened, mycoheterotrophic orchid that obtains nutrients through fungal parasitism
rather than photosynthesis. We will also see our state mushroom Devil’s Cigar or *Chorioactis
geaster* which is also fruiting after the recent rains! We will be collecting it for further
research.

**📅 Saturday, July 25, 2026 🕛 9:00 a.m. 💜 $15+ Donation**

[ Guest Tickets ][140]

## Our mission is to strengthen the conservation, research, and study of Fungi in Central Texas

We are a [member-supported][141], volunteer-run group of united Central Texans dedicated to working
with fungi. Fungi are foundational species for nearly all terrestrial life on Earth—critical links
between the health, stability, and abundance of the soil, plants, and fresh water on which human and
animal life depends. The Central Texas Mycological Society is committed to bringing forth the
recognition of mycology and the Fungal Kingdom as a beneficial ally in the effort to restore and
sustain the resilience of the natural world.

[ Get Map ][142]
[ Volunteer ][143]

SporeCorps is our **indoor cultivation and community lab program** — a hands-on space for curious
minds to explore the science, art, and discipline of growing fungi. SporeCorps teaches indoor STEM
methods in a supportive, futuristic, DIY-lab environment. Join us both online and in-person in labs
in Austin and San Antonio. [Contact us][144] if you want us to teach a class.

# AUSTIN: Orchid Mycology Walk

Join us for a guided nature walk to observe the **Glass Mountain Crested Coralroot** (*Bletia
nitida*)—a threatened, mycoheterotrophic orchid that obtains nutrients through fungal parasitism
rather than photosynthesis. We will also see our state mushroom Devil’s Cigar or *Chorioactis
geaster* which is also fruiting after the recent rains! We will be collecting it for further
research.

**📅 Saturday, July 25, 2026 🕛 9:00 a.m. 💜 $15+ Donation**

[ Guest Tickets ][140]

## Our mission is to strengthen the conservation, research, and study of Fungi in Central Texas

We are a [member-supported][141], volunteer-run group of united Central Texans dedicated to working
with fungi. Fungi are foundational species for nearly all terrestrial life on Earth—critical links
between the health, stability, and abundance of the soil, plants, and fresh water on which human and
animal life depends. The Central Texas Mycological Society is committed to bringing forth the
recognition of mycology and the Fungal Kingdom as a beneficial ally in the effort to restore and
sustain the resilience of the natural world.

[ Get Map ][142]
[ Volunteer ][143]

SporeCorps is our **indoor cultivation and community lab program** — a hands-on space for curious
minds to explore the science, art, and discipline of growing fungi. SporeCorps teaches indoor STEM
methods in a supportive, futuristic, DIY-lab environment. Join us both online and in-person in labs
in Austin and San Antonio. [Contact us][144] if you want us to teach a class.

# Vegan recipes for a healthy life and healthy planet

Clean Green Simple is a plant-based resource for people interested in eating mindfully, living
sustainably, and enjoying life’s simple pleasures. We offer plant-based recipes and nutrition tips,
as well as reviews and buying guides for eco-friendly kitchen, home, and health products.

Wherever you are on your plant-based journey—from plant-curious to 100% vegan— my crew and I are
here to provide you a judgment-free zone that will help empower you to adopt a plant-centric
lifestyle.

We’re excited for the future of 2026! We will soon be offering a convenient mobile app so you can
connect seamlessly to our resources where ever you may be. A membership based meal planning program,
new authors from around the world bringing international flavor to the vegan lifestyle and even a
small commerce section offering uniquely branded T shirt designs showing your vegan pride.

# Vegan recipes for a healthy life and healthy planet

Clean Green Simple is a plant-based resource for people interested in eating mindfully, living
sustainably, and enjoying life’s simple pleasures. We offer plant-based recipes and nutrition tips,
as well as reviews and buying guides for eco-friendly kitchen, home, and health products.

Wherever you are on your plant-based journey—from plant-curious to 100% vegan— my crew and I are
here to provide you a judgment-free zone that will help empower you to adopt a plant-centric
lifestyle.

We’re excited for the future of 2026! We will soon be offering a convenient mobile app so you can
connect seamlessly to our resources where ever you may be. A membership based meal planning program,
new authors from around the world bringing international flavor to the vegan lifestyle and even a
small commerce section offering uniquely branded T shirt designs showing your vegan pride.

products, skin care and cosmetics, household products and water treatment system.

# WELCOME TO WILD FOOD HEAVEN

*Eating wild food helps to restore the connection between humans and nature**
**Explore this site for free in-depth information on wild food, or to book foraging walks, webinars
and mentoring*

[
See all events forward
][49]

## Upcoming events

[

### The Coastal Forager - Summer Coast, Hedgerow and Woodland Foraging Walk with Wild Food Picnic C,
### Galloway

26 July 2026
A guided foray exploring delicious and healthy midsummer wild foods of Galloway's coast, hedgerows
and woods.  Enjoy a wild food tasting picnic in a beautiful location afterwards. Gift vouchers are
available for this event.


][50]
[

### The Coastal Forager - August Sailing and Foraging Week, NW Scotland

1 August 2026
A week of foraging and sailing around the islands and sea lochs of Scotland’s spectacular West
Coast.


][51]
[

### Fungi Foraging Walk & Wild Food Picnic 1, Galloway, SW Scotland

9 August 2026
A guided forage exploring the fascinating world of wild fungi with Scotland's leading wild food
educator. Enjoy a fungi-themed wild food tasting picnic in the forest afterwards. Gift vouchers
available.


][52]
[
Go to blog forward
][53]

## Seasonal Tips from Mark

[

### The Coastal Forager - Buy the Book

A guide to the edible opportunities of North Atlantic coastlines; covering coastal plants, seaweed,
shellfish and more.


][54]
[

### Pineapple Weed - Identification, Edibility, Distribution, Ecology, Recipes

A common, easily recognisable and rather wonderful little "weed", with a delicious aroma of
pineapple and chamomile and lots of sweet and savoury uses in the kitchen


][55]
[

### Chanterelles: Sustainable and Considerate Harvesting

Take a deep dive into the subtleties, science and ethics of harvesting chanterelle mushrooms


][56]
 
[

### Marsh Samphire - Identification, Edibility, Distribution

I have a love-hate relationship with marsh samphire. Mostly its love - the wide open seascapes where
it thrives, its odd cactus-like appearance and its wonderful salty-fresh succulence. Even the silty,
squelchy estuarine habitat where it grows has a "mud-glorious-mud" gooeyness that appeals to the
filthy schoolboy in me.


][57]
[

### Dulse - Identification, Edibility, Distribution

Though not strong in flavour, dulse is one of the stars of the seaweed world - a clinically proven
antioxidant and source of protein, potassium and iodine, making it an excellent treatment for
hypothyroid problems...


][58]
[

### Elderflower Champagne and other Wild Floral Champagnes Recipe

If there is a tastier, more refreshing, easier to make summer drink than this, please let me know!


][59]

# WELCOME TO WILD FOOD HEAVEN

*Eating wild food helps to restore the connection between humans and nature**
**Explore this site for free in-depth information on wild food, or to book foraging walks, webinars
and mentoring*

[
See all events forward
][49]

## Upcoming events

[

### The Coastal Forager - Summer Coast, Hedgerow and Woodland Foraging Walk with Wild Food Picnic C,
### Galloway

26 July 2026
A guided foray exploring delicious and healthy midsummer wild foods of Galloway's coast, hedgerows
and woods.  Enjoy a wild food tasting picnic in a beautiful location afterwards. Gift vouchers are
available for this event.


][50]
[

### The Coastal Forager - August Sailing and Foraging Week, NW Scotland

1 August 2026
A week of foraging and sailing around the islands and sea lochs of Scotland’s spectacular West
Coast.


][51]
[

### Fungi Foraging Walk & Wild Food Picnic 1, Galloway, SW Scotland

9 August 2026
A guided forage exploring the fascinating world of wild fungi with Scotland's leading wild food
educator. Enjoy a fungi-themed wild food tasting picnic in the forest afterwards. Gift vouchers
available.


][52]
[
Go to blog forward
][53]

## Seasonal Tips from Mark

[

### The Coastal Forager - Buy the Book

A guide to the edible opportunities of North Atlantic coastlines; covering coastal plants, seaweed,
shellfish and more.


][54]
[

### Pineapple Weed - Identification, Edibility, Distribution, Ecology, Recipes

A common, easily recognisable and rather wonderful little "weed", with a delicious aroma of
pineapple and chamomile and lots of sweet and savoury uses in the kitchen


][55]
[

### Chanterelles: Sustainable and Considerate Harvesting

Take a deep dive into the subtleties, science and ethics of harvesting chanterelle mushrooms


][56]
 
[

### Marsh Samphire - Identification, Edibility, Distribution

I have a love-hate relationship with marsh samphire. Mostly its love - the wide open seascapes where
it thrives, its odd cactus-like appearance and its wonderful salty-fresh succulence. Even the silty,
squelchy estuarine habitat where it grows has a "mud-glorious-mud" gooeyness that appeals to the
filthy schoolboy in me.


][57]
[

### Dulse - Identification, Edibility, Distribution

Though not strong in flavour, dulse is one of the stars of the seaweed world - a clinically proven
antioxidant and source of protein, potassium and iodine, making it an excellent treatment for
hypothyroid problems...


][58]
[

### Elderflower Champagne and other Wild Floral Champagnes Recipe

If there is a tastier, more refreshing, easier to make summer drink than this, please let me know!


][59]

Established in 1996, Guan’s Mushroom is a leading grower and distributor of fresh specialty
mushrooms in North America, with three farms in California and five distribution centers located in
San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York, West Grove and Toronto.

#### Our Proprietary

# Elevation Technology®

**Elevating Product Experience with Clear, Odorless Emulsions, featuring:**

**Clear, Odorless Emulsions**: Creates flawless emulsions for finished products.

**Nano-Sized Droplets (<80 nm)**: Encapsulates high-quality lipophilic actives in stable nano-sized
droplets, ensuring increased absorption and enhanced bioavailability.

**Industry-Leading Stability**: Combines nano emulsification technologies with custom machinery and
proprietary processes for stable active emulsions.

**Consistent Effects**: Delivers rapid, predictable, and consistent effects.

**Thermodynamically and Kinetically Stable**: The nano-sized droplets are stable, enhancing the
product's effectiveness.

**Stackable and Predictable Formulations**: Ensures a consistent experience with each use.

Elevation Technology® plays a crucial role in generating a Novel Chemical Entity (NCE) by creating
unique and stable nano-emulsions that improve the bioavailability and efficacy of active
ingredients. This proprietary technology allows for the precise formulation of cannabinoids and
other compounds into new, patentable forms, effectively transforming them into NCEs.

By enhancing the solubility, stability, and absorption rates of these compounds, Elevation
Technology® not only improves the therapeutic potential but also meets the rigorous standards
required for pharmaceutical applications. This innovative approach positions HYTN at the forefront
of cannabinoid-based pharmaceutical development, offering new opportunities for specialized
formulations and targeted therapeutic applications.

  Jason holds an [M.Sc][70]. in Molecular Genetics and brings over 15 years of experience in the
  pharmaceutical industry. His career includes a tenure as head of the RX Division for a leading
  dermatology company. With expertise spanning medical devices, pharmaceuticals, fertility, and
  cannabis industries, Jason has built and led operational, regulatory, and quality systems. Prior
  to joining HYTN, he co-founded The Flowr Corporation (TSXV: FLWR), where he served as SVP -
  Operations and Chief Research and Innovation Officer.
  
  
  Prior to joining HYTN Jason co- founded and served as SVP - Operations and Chief Research and

#### Our Proprietary

# Elevation Technology®

**Elevating Product Experience with Clear, Odorless Emulsions, featuring:**

**Clear, Odorless Emulsions**: Creates flawless emulsions for finished products.

**Nano-Sized Droplets (<80 nm)**: Encapsulates high-quality lipophilic actives in stable nano-sized
droplets, ensuring increased absorption and enhanced bioavailability.

**Industry-Leading Stability**: Combines nano emulsification technologies with custom machinery and
proprietary processes for stable active emulsions.

**Consistent Effects**: Delivers rapid, predictable, and consistent effects.

**Thermodynamically and Kinetically Stable**: The nano-sized droplets are stable, enhancing the
product's effectiveness.

**Stackable and Predictable Formulations**: Ensures a consistent experience with each use.

Elevation Technology® plays a crucial role in generating a Novel Chemical Entity (NCE) by creating
unique and stable nano-emulsions that improve the bioavailability and efficacy of active
ingredients. This proprietary technology allows for the precise formulation of cannabinoids and
other compounds into new, patentable forms, effectively transforming them into NCEs.

By enhancing the solubility, stability, and absorption rates of these compounds, Elevation
Technology® not only improves the therapeutic potential but also meets the rigorous standards
required for pharmaceutical applications. This innovative approach positions HYTN at the forefront
of cannabinoid-based pharmaceutical development, offering new opportunities for specialized
formulations and targeted therapeutic applications.

When consumed regularly in as whole mushrooms encompassing the complete range of bioactive
compounds, these organisms have shown promise in supporting various aspects of cognition, including
memory, focus, mood and overall brain health. M2 leverages this scientific understanding, offering
both individual species and custom, proprietary blends designed to optimize cognitive health .

chitin, 2 major carbohydrates found in all mushrooms are known as prebiotics. Clinical evidence of
the benefits of functional mushrooms on digestive health is mounting and led M2 to invest in this

significantly fostered the growth of beneficial gut bacteria, leading to a cascade of positive

positive shift in microbial species diversity. Beyond these core prebiotic effects, the study also
revealed metabolic outcomes linked to the mushrooms, indicating modulation of various neuroactive
metabolites, suggesting a potential connection between gut health and neurological function.

ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE

M2’s whole mushroom Cordyceps can positively impact athletic performance by enhancing the body’s
ability to utilize oxygen. A study published in the Journal of the International Society of Sports
Nutrition demonstrated that consistent intake of a mushroom blend containing Cordyceps significantly
increased maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max) and time to exhaustion during high-intensity
exercise.

 

Athletes using Cordyceps may experience improved endurance and delayed fatigue. Our mushrooms help
the body more efficiently deliver oxygen to muscles, allowing for sustained and potentially more
powerful physical activity. While not all results reached statistical significance, there was also a
trend toward increased ventilatory threshold and peak power output, further suggesting that
Cordyceps can be a valuable natural supplement for enhancing athletic performance.

THE M2 DIFFERENCE – WHOLE MUSHROOM POWDERS

## FULL LIFE CYCLE MATTERS

[LEARN MORE][22]

SCIENCE-BACKED

## ORGANIC WHOLE MUSHROOMS

Unlock the power of the full life cycle

Derived from the entire organism (mycelium and fruiting body), whole mushroom products offer
superior benefits compared to extracts or powders solely from the fruiting body. This is because the
mycelium contains a diverse array of bioactive compounds. By utilizing the entire organism, whole
mushroom powders provide a more comprehensive and potent source of functional compounds, maximizing
the potential health benefits for functional applications.

[ LEARN MORE ][23]
[mushroom closeup image]

GROWN IN SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA

## US GROWN + VERTICALLY INTEGRATED

M2 Ingredients maintains complete control over quality and consistency by cultivating all our
mushrooms within our expansive, 155,000 sq ft., Organic and BRCGS Certified facility in Southern
California. From strain development to final shipment, every stage – substrate storage and
hydration, cultivation of the full lifecycle, drying and milling– occurs in a meticulously
controlled environment, controlling for contaminants and ensuring quality. Our comprehensive,
on-site operations in Vista, CA, include harvesting, drying, and storage, guaranteeing a seamless
chain of custody. We offer unparalleled customer support, providing direct access to our expert
mycologists, FSQA professionals, and food scientists, empowering your team every step of the way. As
a fully domestic operation, we are also immune to import tariffs, ensuring a reliable and
transparent supply chain for our customers, while our expansive facility allows us to meet the
growing demands of the industry.

[ CONTACT US ][24]
[forklift and operator]

## AS FEATURED IN

[ [Food Business News Logo] ][25] [ [Food Navigator Logo] ][26] [ [Food Engineering logo] ][27] [
[yahoo finance logo] ][28] [ [nosh logo] ][29] [ [NutraIngredients logo] ][30] [ [Keri-Report logo]
][31]

BORN OF SHARED VISION & COMMITMENT TO EXCELLENCE

## OUR JOURNEY

M2 Ingredients was born from a powerful combination: a passion for mycology, expertise for mushroom
cultivation, and a commitment to preventative health. This unique blend of expertise has propelled
us to become North America’s largest grower of functional mushrooms, setting a standard for the
industry. We’ve stayed true to our founding principles, building state-of-the-art, certified organic
facilities and investing in rigorous scientific research. Our commitment to uncompromising quality
is evident in our adherence to the highest standards within the sector. At M2 Ingredients, we
deliver the highest quality, most effective mushroom ingredients, backed by both deep-rooted
knowledge and cutting-edge science.

2010
[Dr. Sandra Carter and Steve Farrar holding mushrooms]

M2 Ingredients, originally founded as Mushroom Matrix by Dr. Sandra Carter and mycologist Steve
Farrar, was built on a foundation of quality, science, and with the promise of growing the best and
most efficacious mushrooms.

2010
[USDA Organic logo]

As pioneers in the functional mushroom space, M2 Ingredients was among the first to achieve USDA
Organic Certification. We believe that producing products that are both beneficial for consumers and
sustainable for the planet is fundamental to our mission.

2011
[M2 logo laid over image of mushrooms]

We rebranded from Mushroom Matrix to ‘M2 Ingredients’ to represent our expansion and leadership in
the functional ingredient space. Mushroom Matrix now lives on as a fantastic pet and equine care
brand, created by our original founders.

2012
[spoons with supplements]

Our mushrooms were first used in a large multinational supplement brand, putting functional
mushrooms on the map for supplement, food, and beverage brands.

2015
[PRiestly Location]

Moved into a new growing location – quadrupling our capacity.

2018
[closeup of cordyceps]

We published our first clinical trial on Cordyceps, which demonstrated that a 4-gram daily dose of a
blend containing *Cordyceps militaris* for three weeks significantly improved physiological markers
of aerobic performance.

2020
[BRCS Food Safety and AA Certified logos]

A BRCGS AA rating, which M2 Ingredients achieved in 2020, signifies top-tier quality and rigorous
food safety standards, crucial for customer confidence in our functional mushrooms.

2024
[overhead view of M2 Ingredients warehouse]

We opened our new, high-capacity, 155,000 sq ft facility in Vista, CA – making us the LARGEST
FUNCTIONAL MUSHROOM GROWER IN THE WESTERN HEMISPHERE. This cutting-edge facility operates around the
clock with multiple shifts, ensuring consistent production and rapid order fulfillment, delivering
greater capacity and quality than ever before.

2025
[The words Regenerative Organic Certified are laid over mushroom image]

M2 Ingredients has expanded its product line to include Regenerative Organic Certified SKUs. This
certification signifies a commitment beyond traditional organic standards, requiring products to
meet the highest benchmarks for organic production while prioritizing environmental regeneration and
social fairness.

M2’s whole mushroom Cordyceps can positively impact athletic performance by enhancing the body’s
ability to utilize oxygen. A study published in the Journal of the International Society of Sports
Nutrition demonstrated that consistent intake of a mushroom blend containing Cordyceps significantly
increased maximal oxygen consumption (VO2 max) and time to exhaustion during high-intensity
exercise.

 

Athletes using Cordyceps may experience improved endurance and delayed fatigue. Our mushrooms help
the body more efficiently deliver oxygen to muscles, allowing for sustained and potentially more
powerful physical activity. While not all results reached statistical significance, there was also a
trend toward increased ventilatory threshold and peak power output, further suggesting that
Cordyceps can be a valuable natural supplement for enhancing athletic performance.

[ LEARN MORE ][21]
[gloved hands holding petri dish]

THE M2 DIFFERENCE – WHOLE MUSHROOM POWDERS

## FULL LIFE CYCLE MATTERS

[LEARN MORE][22]

SCIENCE-BACKED

## ORGANIC WHOLE MUSHROOMS

Unlock the power of the full life cycle

Derived from the entire organism (mycelium and fruiting body), whole mushroom products offer
superior benefits compared to extracts or powders solely from the fruiting body. This is because the
mycelium contains a diverse array of bioactive compounds. By utilizing the entire organism, whole
mushroom powders provide a more comprehensive and potent source of functional compounds, maximizing
the potential health benefits for functional applications.

[ LEARN MORE ][23]
[mushroom closeup image]

GROWN IN SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA

## US GROWN + VERTICALLY INTEGRATED

M2 Ingredients maintains complete control over quality and consistency by cultivating all our
mushrooms within our expansive, 155,000 sq ft., Organic and BRCGS Certified facility in Southern
California. From strain development to final shipment, every stage – substrate storage and
hydration, cultivation of the full lifecycle, drying and milling– occurs in a meticulously
controlled environment, controlling for contaminants and ensuring quality. Our comprehensive,
on-site operations in Vista, CA, include harvesting, drying, and storage, guaranteeing a seamless
chain of custody. We offer unparalleled customer support, providing direct access to our expert
mycologists, FSQA professionals, and food scientists, empowering your team every step of the way. As
a fully domestic operation, we are also immune to import tariffs, ensuring a reliable and
transparent supply chain for our customers, while our expansive facility allows us to meet the
growing demands of the industry.

[ CONTACT US ][24]

BORN OF SHARED VISION & COMMITMENT TO EXCELLENCE

## OUR JOURNEY

M2 Ingredients was born from a powerful combination: a passion for mycology, expertise for mushroom
cultivation, and a commitment to preventative health. This unique blend of expertise has propelled
us to become North America’s largest grower of functional mushrooms, setting a standard for the
industry. We’ve stayed true to our founding principles, building state-of-the-art, certified organic
facilities and investing in rigorous scientific research. Our commitment to uncompromising quality
is evident in our adherence to the highest standards within the sector. At M2 Ingredients, we
deliver the highest quality, most effective mushroom ingredients, backed by both deep-rooted
knowledge and cutting-edge science.

2010
[Dr. Sandra Carter and Steve Farrar holding mushrooms]

M2 Ingredients, originally founded as Mushroom Matrix by Dr. Sandra Carter and mycologist Steve
Farrar, was built on a foundation of quality, science, and with the promise of growing the best and
most efficacious mushrooms.

2010
[USDA Organic logo]

As pioneers in the functional mushroom space, M2 Ingredients was among the first to achieve USDA
Organic Certification. We believe that producing products that are both beneficial for consumers and
sustainable for the planet is fundamental to our mission.

2011
[M2 logo laid over image of mushrooms]

We rebranded from Mushroom Matrix to ‘M2 Ingredients’ to represent our expansion and leadership in
the functional ingredient space. Mushroom Matrix now lives on as a fantastic pet and equine care
brand, created by our original founders.

2012
[spoons with supplements]

Our mushrooms were first used in a large multinational supplement brand, putting functional
mushrooms on the map for supplement, food, and beverage brands.

2015
[PRiestly Location]

Moved into a new growing location – quadrupling our capacity.

2018
[closeup of cordyceps]

We published our first clinical trial on Cordyceps, which demonstrated that a 4-gram daily dose of a
blend containing *Cordyceps militaris* for three weeks significantly improved physiological markers
of aerobic performance.

2020
[BRCS Food Safety and AA Certified logos]

A BRCGS AA rating, which M2 Ingredients achieved in 2020, signifies top-tier quality and rigorous
food safety standards, crucial for customer confidence in our functional mushrooms.

2024
[overhead view of M2 Ingredients warehouse]

We opened our new, high-capacity, 155,000 sq ft facility in Vista, CA – making us the LARGEST
FUNCTIONAL MUSHROOM GROWER IN THE WESTERN HEMISPHERE. This cutting-edge facility operates around the
clock with multiple shifts, ensuring consistent production and rapid order fulfillment, delivering
greater capacity and quality than ever before.

2025
[The words Regenerative Organic Certified are laid over mushroom image]

M2 Ingredients has expanded its product line to include Regenerative Organic Certified SKUs. This
certification signifies a commitment beyond traditional organic standards, requiring products to
meet the highest benchmarks for organic production while prioritizing environmental regeneration and
social fairness.

**The World of Mushroom From Spawn to Plate**

[Contact][2]
[Support][3]

#### Our Journey So Far
1. **Established a Visually Challenged Youth Managed Mushroom Farming Centre**: Choto Shalbari,
   Coochbehar, West Bengal
2. **Set up a Mushroom Processing Unit and Work Hostel:** Sheoraphuli, Hooghly, West Bengal (HQ of
   MushroomAg)
3. **Empowered Visually Challenged Youth and Marginal Farmer**s:
*   Engaged with 100+ visually challenged youth as part of the founding and beneficiary ecosystem
*   Supported and backward integrated 300+ marginal mushroom farmers

## MUSHROOMERS is the brand name of MushroomAg Private Limited

We're passionate about harnessing the power of sustainable agriculture to drive positive change. Our
pioneering approach combines cutting-edge technology with social impact, empowering marginal farmers
and differently abled youth to thrive. 

## MushroomAg Products

MushroomAg Product Catalogue

[Download PDF][4]

## About Us

#### Our Mission

We're revolutionizing the mushroom industry by creating a sustainable ecosystem that supports
marginalized farmers, visually challenged, and differently abled youth. Our goal is to make
high-protein, nutritious mushroom-based products accessible to all.



#### Our Initiatives
* Developing a Technology-Enabled Platform for Mushroom Farming Lifecycle and Agribusiness Ecosystem
  Management
* Organic mushroom cultivation (presently 5 farming units) with plans to set up 40 mushroom farming
  polyhouses
* Procurement of raw mushrooms from trained marginal farmers
* Mushroom-based processed products (mushroom chips, protein bars, crispies, jerkies, dried
  mushrooms)
* Setting up a Mushroom-Based New Food Product and Processing Unit
* Providing mushroom training to local marginal farmers



#### The Problem We're Solving
* Limited availability of high-protein meat substitutes for vegetarians and vegans
* Seasonal availability of mushrooms due to lack of large-scale cultivation and spawn
* Limited varieties of mushrooms and high-protein snacks
* High prices and limited outlets for mushrooms



#### Our Solutions
* Mass production of mushrooms through backward integration with marginalized farmers and FPOs
* Affordable, commercial-quality spawn production
* Growing 8-9 varieties of mushrooms with minimal investment
* Setting up commercially viable processing units for mushroom-based products
* Creating multiple channels for delivery and increasing outlets through engagement of visually
  challenged and differently abled youth



#### Testimonials
* TotalStart, Accel Partners, Hughes Systique, and others are excited about our steady progress and
  willing to support our efforts for the next several years through their differently abled
  engagement action program.
* They have been supporting us for the last 4 years to help build the organization.



#### What's Next?
* **Building a Mushroom Farming Lifecycle Management Solution**: With visually challenged youth at
  the core, engaging all players to provide inputs to marginalized mushroom farmers and sell their
  output.
* **We Need Your Suppor**t: Join us in empowering visually challenged youth and marginal farmers,
  and creating a sustainable mushroom farming ecosystem.

## Collaborating for Agricultural Excellence

#### MushroomAg Private Limited Partners with ABIF IIT KGP

MushroomAg Private Limited is delighted to announce a landmark partnership with Agri Business
Incubation Foundation IIT Kharagpur (ABIF IIT KGP), solidified through a Memorandum of Understanding
(MOU). This strategic collaboration marks a significant milestone in our journey, and we extend our
gratitude to TotalStart for their unwavering support.  Together, we are committed to creating a
sustainable and inclusive agricultural ecosystem, and we look forward to achieving remarkable
outcomes through this partnership.

## Update on Blind Youth Engagement & Easter Invitation

#### Celebrate Easter & Collaborate with TotalStart

This Easter, join the TotalStart community in our mission to drive meaningful social impact and
create a brighter future for all. As we celebrate the renewal and hope that comes with this special
day, we invite you to be a part of our collaborative efforts to address some of the world's most
pressing challenges.

By joining our community, you'll become part of a vibrant network of changemakers, entrepreneurs,
and innovators working together to:

 - Develop and scale sustainable agricultural practices

 - Support inclusive entrepreneurship and job creation

        - Foster collaborative partnerships and knowledge sharing

- Drive policy change and advocacy for social impact

## About Us

#### Our Mission

We're revolutionizing the mushroom industry by creating a sustainable ecosystem that supports
marginalized farmers, visually challenged, and differently abled youth. Our goal is to make
high-protein, nutritious mushroom-based products accessible to all.



#### Our Initiatives
* Developing a Technology-Enabled Platform for Mushroom Farming Lifecycle and Agribusiness Ecosystem
  Management
* Organic mushroom cultivation (presently 5 farming units) with plans to set up 40 mushroom farming
  polyhouses
* Procurement of raw mushrooms from trained marginal farmers
* Mushroom-based processed products (mushroom chips, protein bars, crispies, jerkies, dried
  mushrooms)
* Setting up a Mushroom-Based New Food Product and Processing Unit
* Providing mushroom training to local marginal farmers



#### The Problem We're Solving
* Limited availability of high-protein meat substitutes for vegetarians and vegans
* Seasonal availability of mushrooms due to lack of large-scale cultivation and spawn
* Limited varieties of mushrooms and high-protein snacks
* High prices and limited outlets for mushrooms



#### Our Solutions
* Mass production of mushrooms through backward integration with marginalized farmers and FPOs
* Affordable, commercial-quality spawn production
* Growing 8-9 varieties of mushrooms with minimal investment
* Setting up commercially viable processing units for mushroom-based products
* Creating multiple channels for delivery and increasing outlets through engagement of visually

# Mushroom FM, the Home of the Fun Guys, with Four Decades of Magic Mushroom Memories

## Currently On Air

Currently on air we have a replay of Airplay Rewind with [Spencer James][24].

## Listen Now right from your browser
* [ Play Mushroom FM][25]

## Vote for your favorite holiday songs

Tell us your top 10 holiday songs, and we'll send you an invitation to our virtual holiday party
where we play the top 100 as voted for by the mushroom crowd. Voting is easy and accessible. [Vote
today! ][39] Tell your friends to do the same! Then tune in at 7 AM Eastern on December 20.

## Welcome

Welcome to Mushroom FM. We're pleased you stopped by.

Mushroom FM is a licensed Internet stream in New Zealand bringing you four decades of magic Mushroom
memories, with music from the 50s to the 80s. When you need something on at work that plays music
everyone's familiar with presented by engaging personalities, when you want to hear a station that
plays songs to make you sing and smile, and all commercial-free with the exception of the occasional
old ad we might play for nostalgia, you've come to the right place.

If you lived the music of the time, you'll appreciate that we go way beyond the usual few gold
tracks you'll hear elsewhere. Our music library is extensive. We care about the quality, so we take
care to choose the full album cuts where we can, and the best masters currently available. Plus, we
sound fantastic on a good audio system.

### The Mushroom FM difference

In an era where you can dial up almost any tune ever recorded, the value we add is in our fun,
friendly on-air team, and in the carefully chosen music selection. When we can, we bring you radio
where the personality makes a difference. When that's not possible, the automated mix from all of
our four decades is fresh and eclectic.

### Your memories are as diverse as our music

Sometimes we get asked if we're an easy listening station, a countries station, a pop station or a
rock station? The answer to that is, yes... We're all those things. We're obsessed with those four
great, influential, transformative decades in music. So if it was recorded then, we'll play it.

Our model for our music format is The Beatles themselves. Were the Beatles a band that recorded
standards, pop hits, heavy rock or show tunes? Well, they did all that and more. So let the music
take you on a magical mystery tour. We predict you're never more than a song or two away from one of
your all-time favourites.

### Join the family

The Mushroom FM family consists of great listeners like you who we affectionately call The Mushroom
Crowd, without whom there'd be no point in it all, as well as our knowledgeable and friendly team of
presenters, who we call the fun guys. Our fun guys are all over the globe, including in New Zealand,
Australia, Britain, South Africa, Canada and the US. We love hearing from you about what we're
doing, what we're saying, and what we're playing.

### No matter where you go, there we are

It's super easy to listen to Mushroom FM, whether you're at home, at the office, or on the move.
Choose the Play Mushroom FM link right on this page. You'll find us in all the good radio apps,
including iTunes, TuneIn, Ootunes, myTuner Radio and many more. We're built right into the Victor
Reader Stream and Leasey Radio as well.

Got an Amazon Echo or a Google Home? We have our very own Alexa skill and Google action. No need to
rely on any third party. Just say, "Alexa, open Mushroom FM", or "Hey Google, ask Mushroom FM to
play".

We're best buds with the assistant on your smartphone as well. Just instruct Siri or Google
Assistant on your phone to "play Mushroom FM".

Sonos? We love Sonos! Search for us there v

Got an Amazon Echo or a Google Home? We have our very own Alexa skill and Google action. No need to
rely on any third party. Just say, "Alexa, open Mushroom FM", or "Hey Google, ask Mushroom FM to
play".

We're best buds with the assistant on your smartphone as well. Just instruct Siri or Google
Assistant on your phone to "play Mushroom FM".

Sonos? We love Sonos! Search for us there via TuneIn or Sonos Radio.

We love engaging with The Mushroom Crowd via social media. The best way to be a part of the
conversation is to use and track our Mastodon hashtag, #MushroomFM. Of course, sometimes it's just
nice to sit back and be entertained, and we love it when listeners do that too.

You can also follow the official [Mushroom FM Mastodon account ][40]for show announcements and other
news, or subscribe to our low-traffic, [announcements-only email list.][41]

### Mushroom FM? What?

Oh, our crazy name? Well the short version is that we wanted to be a fun thing to be a part of, and
a fun thing to listen to. So after deciding that we wanted to be the fun guys, Mushroom FM seemed a
natural name. Get it? Mushroomn? Fun guys? ...

So settle back, crank it up, and enjoy the best four decades music ever produced, because Mushroom
FM is your home for four decades of magic Mushroom memories.

[And when you need to escape into a world of classic drama and comedy, be sure to check out our
second channel, Mushroom Escape.][42]

## Vote for your favorite holiday songs

Tell us your top 10 holiday songs, and we'll send you an invitation to our virtual holiday party
where we play the top 100 as voted for by the mushroom crowd. Voting is easy and accessible. [Vote
today! ][39] Tell your friends to do the same! Then tune in at 7 AM Eastern on December 20.

## Welcome

Welcome to Mushroom FM. We're pleased you stopped by.

Mushroom FM is a licensed Internet stream in New Zealand bringing you four decades of magic Mushroom
memories, with music from the 50s to the 80s. When you need something on at work that plays music
everyone's familiar with presented by engaging personalities, when you want to hear a station that
plays songs to make you sing and smile, and all commercial-free with the exception of the occasional
old ad we might play for nostalgia, you've come to the right place.

If you lived the music of the time, you'll appreciate that we go way beyond the usual few gold
tracks you'll hear elsewhere. Our music library is extensive. We care about the quality, so we take
care to choose the full album cuts where we can, and the best masters currently available. Plus, we
sound fantastic on a good audio system.

### The Mushroom FM difference

In an era where you can dial up almost any tune ever recorded, the value we add is in our fun,
friendly on-air team, and in the carefully chosen music selection. When we can, we bring you radio
where the personality makes a difference. When that's not possible, the automated mix from all of
our four decades is fresh and eclectic.

### Your memories are as diverse as our music

Sometimes we get asked if we're an easy listening station, a countries station, a pop station or a
rock station? The answer to that is, yes... We're all those things. We're obsessed with those four
great, influential, transformative decades in music. So if it was recorded then, we'll play it.

Our model for our music format is The Beatles themselves. Were the Beatles a band that recorded
standards, pop hits, heavy rock or show tunes? Well, they did all that and more. So let the music
take you on a magical mystery tour. We predict you're never more than a song or two away from one of
your all-time favourites.

### Join the family

The Mushroom FM family consists of great listeners like you who we affectionately call The Mushroom
Crowd, without whom there'd be no point in it all, as well as our knowledgeable and friendly team of
presenters, who we call the fun guys. Our fun guys are all over the globe, including in New Zealand,
Australia, Britain, South Africa, Canada and the US. We love hearing from you about what we're
doing, what we're saying, and what we're playing.

### No matter where you go, there we are

It's super easy to listen to Mushroom FM, whether you're at home, at the office, or on the move.
Choose the Play Mushroom FM link right on this page. You'll find us in all the good radio apps,
including iTunes, TuneIn, Ootunes, myTuner Radio and many more. We're built right into the Victor
Reader Stream and Leasey Radio as well.

Got an Amazon Echo or a Google Home? We have our very own Alexa skill and Google action. No need to
rely on any third party. Just say, "Alexa, open Mushroom FM", or "Hey Google, ask Mushroom FM to
play".

We're best buds with the assistant on your smartphone as well. Just instruct Siri or Google
Assistant on your phone to "play Mushroom FM".

Sonos? We love Sonos! Search for us there via TuneIn or Sonos Radio.

We love engaging with The Mushroom Crowd via social media. The best way to be a part of the
conversation is to use and track our Mastodon hashtag, #MushroomFM. Of course, sometimes it's just
nice to sit back and be entertained, and we love it when listeners do that too.

You can also follow the official [Mushroom FM Mastodon account ][40]for show announcements and other
news, or subscribe to our low-traffic, [announcements-only email list.][41]

### Mushroom FM? What?

Oh, our crazy name? Well the short version is that we wanted to be a fun thing to be a part of, and
a fun thing to listen to. So after deciding that we wanted to be the fun guys, Mushroom FM seemed a
natural name. Get it? Mushroomn? Fun guys? ...

So settle back, crank it up, and enjoy the best four decades music ever produced, because Mushroom
FM is your home for four decades of magic Mushroom memories.

[And when you need to escape into a world of classic drama and comedy, be sure to check out our
second channel, Mushroom Escape.][42]

This identification tool is for informational and educational purposes only and may be inaccurate.

* Unlimited Identifications

Start Now

## How to use Mushroom Identifier
1. 1
   
   ### Upload Multiple Angles
   
   Click "Upload Images" to add up to 6 photos. Capture the cap from above, the full side profile,
   and the base emerging from the ground. More angles mean a more accurate match.
2. 2
   
   ### Photograph the Underside
   
   Flip the cap to show what's beneath — gills, pores, or teeth. This single view is often the
   fastest way to narrow the species. Tip: a photo in the shade reduces glare on the gills.
3. 3
   
   ### Set the Date Found
   
   Update the Date Found field to the day you spotted it. Seasonality is a key identifier — many
   species fruit only in spring, summer, or fall, so timing helps rule out look-alikes.
4. 4
   
   ### Add Location & Habitat Context
   
   Enter where it was found — a town, park, or trail name is enough. Note nearby trees, ground
   cover, or whether it was growing on wood or soil. Habitat is often as important as the photo
   itself.
5. 5
   
   ### Review Results & Stay Safe
   
   Press "Identify Mushroom" to start the analysis and review your results. Use them as a starting
   point only — never make edibility decisions based on an AI result alone. When in doubt, consult a
   local mycologist.

## How a Mushroom Identifier Works

A modern **mushroom identifier** uses artificial intelligence trained on hundreds of thousands of
labeled fungal specimens. When you upload an image, the system extracts visual features — cap shape,
color, surface texture, gill pattern, stem structure — and compares them against a database of known
species to return a ranked list of likely matches.

What separates a reliable **mushroom identifier** from a basic image search is context-awareness.
The AI does not simply look at color in isolation; it weighs combinations of structural traits
together. A brown cap with free gills and a stem ring tells a very different story than a brown cap
with decurrent gills and no ring. These compound patterns allow the model to distinguish species
that look nearly identical at a glance.

Location and seasonality data sharpen accuracy further. Many fungi share overlapping ranges, so
knowing whether a specimen appeared in a Pacific Northwest conifer forest versus a Midwestern oak
woodland meaningfully narrows the candidate pool.

Keep in mind that results reflect visual probability, not certainty. The same species can look
dramatically different depending on age, moisture, and elevation. Think of an AI result as the kind
of working hypothesis an experienced forager would form in the first few minutes of careful
observation — a strong starting point that still needs to be checked against spore print color,
bruising reactions, smell, and, when in doubt, advice from a qualified local expert.

## What Photos Produce the Most Accurate Mushroom Identification

The quality and variety of your images are the single biggest factor in getting a precise result
from a **mushroom identifier**. A single overhead shot of the cap rarely contains enough information
to distinguish species confidently. A comprehensive set of photos takes about two minutes to capture
and makes a substantial difference in accuracy.

**Start with the cap.** Photograph it from directly above in natural, even light — overcast days are
ideal because harsh sunlight creates shadows that obscure surface detail. Then crouch to capture a
full side profile showing how the cap edge curls, lifts, or droops.

**Turn the mushroom over.** The underside — gills, pores, spines, or wrinkles — is frequently the
most diagnostic feature of the entire specimen. Get close enough to show the attachment point where
the gills or pores meet the stem.

**Photograph the stem base.** Dig gently around the base before pulling the mushroom out. Some
species have a cup-shaped volva or basal bulb that is completely hidden at ground level. Missing
this detail can lead to a misread, particularly with *Amanita* species.

**Include a habitat frame.** Step back and capture the mushroom in context: surrounding leaf litter,
nearby tree trunks, log substrate, or moss. This environmental view is often as revealing as the
specimen itself, especially when paired with a location note.

## The Role of Habitat in Mushroom Identification

Fungi do not exist in isolation. Nearly every mushroom species has evolved a specific ecological
relationship — with particular tree families, soil types, decaying wood, or living root systems —
and those relationships are essential context for narrowing down what you have found.

Mycorrhizal species form underground partnerships with trees. **Chanterelles**, for example, are
almost always found near oaks, beeches, or conifers, depending on the region. A look-alike growing
in a grassy field far from any trees is almost certainly something different. Noting the dominant
tree species within ten meters of your find is one of the most valuable pieces of information you
can provide.

Substrate matters just as much. A mushroom growing directly from a living oak tree is in a
completely different candidate pool from one growing from buried roots, decaying hardwood logs, or
open soil. Wood-rotting species, soil-dwelling species, and dung-loving species rarely overlap, even
when they appear superficially similar.

Elevation and climate add another layer. A specimen found at 8,000 feet in a Rocky Mountain spruce
forest is unlikely to be the same species as one found in the humid lowlands of Louisiana, even if
both share a similar appearance.

When using a **mushroom identifier**, adding a location and noting the immediate surroundings — even
a brief phrase like "base of a dead birch" or "open meadow, Rocky Mountains" — consistently produces
more precise matches than images alone.

## Understanding the Limits of AI Mushroom Identification

A **mushroom identifier** powered by AI is a powerful first step, but understanding its limitations
is as important as knowing how to use it well. Visual similarity between species is a fundamental

## Mushroom Spray Machine

**Significance**
* A number of infections, especially the dangerous *Trichoderma*, can spread through the spray water
  used on mushrooms.
* Very hot or cold water damages mushroom mycelium and affects its smooth growth.
* This system pasteurizes, conditions, and sprays water to protect mushrooms from infections
  originating from water sources.
* Regardless of whether the water source is groundwater or municipal supply, it consistently
  supports better mushroom growth.

**Function**
* Used in automatic and semi-automatic modes for all types of mushrooms.
* Pasteurization of water.
* Water conditioning.
* Uniform spraying system.
* Maintains stable humidity levels of **80–85%**.

**Benefits**
* Eliminates the need for expensive RO water purification plants.
* Consumes less electricity, ensuring minimal operating cost per cycle.

**Material & Components**
* Pasteurization system capable of processing **250 liters of water per cycle**.
* Spraying system supporting **1 to 20 spray trees**, each with **6 tiers**, operating together.

# The World's First Gesture-Controlled Singing Bowl System!

[Buy Now ][19]
[MusicalMushroomAdR.png]

#### @margofreemusic

"I absolutely love the performance delivery with the musical mushrooms! I am able to demonstrate my
creativity singing with my crystal bowls in a completely unique and engaging way. I really
appreciate the full “stop” of sound when I dramatically wave my hands over the bowls to allow for
that moment of sacred pause. Everyone is held in suspenseful silence before my voice and the bowls
come softly back in… it is an experience like no other that never was achievable with mallets. Thank
you Musical Mushroom!" - Margo Free, Vocalist & EDM/Sound Healing Producer

#### @shamanictonic

""The Musical Mushroom has been a game changer for me as a sound practitioner. It allows me to drone
lower octaves while I play higher-octave bowls or other instruments—creating a depth of sound that
feels like having a second practitioner playing alongside me. Participants consistently comment on
how impactful the intervals and triads feel. I also use the Musical Mushrooms in one-on-one
sessions, placing them beneath the table so clients can feel and hear the vibrations as I work with
bowls and tuning forks. The experience adds a powerful somatic dimension to the session and deepens
the overall therapeutic effect." - Sonia Stingo - Professional Sound Practitioner

## Our Story

Changing the Game

Vibrational sound healing instruments such as singing bowls, gongs and bells have been around for
thousands of years and used in many different cultures both for healing and ritual purposes.  The
way these instruments have been played has remained mostly unchanged during this time.  We believe
that the digital era we live in has enabled new technologies which can be harnessed to enhance these
time-honored instruments while preserving their traditional essence.  Our mission is to introduce
new technologies aimed at enhancing the experience while making these instruments accessible to a
broader group of practitioners in an effort to help raise our global vibrations. 

"The best way to predict the future is to create it"

## Abraham Lincoln

[A stack of Musical Mushroom automated singing bowl controllers on a table.]

## Our Technology

A new Interaction Paradigm

Our patent pending flagship product, the Musical Mushroom®, enables sound practitioners to control
their singing bowls or similar resonant instruments using simple hand gestures using a small
removable exciter coil glued to the inside surface of the bowl.  This new approach replaces the use
of the traditional mallet.  Electro-mechanical vibrations excite the bowl at its resonant
frequencies under the guidance of the performer, whether in close proximity using hand gestures or
via wired (USB) control using the MIDI protocol.  One of the many benefits of replacing the mallet
includes the ability to physically extend the performer's range, as well as to automatically hold a
drone note while the performer is free to simultaneously play other bowls or instruments.

[Illustration of how the Musical Mushroom works in a crystal singing bowl]

A novel hand gesture sensor enables local interactions using the performer's hands hovering over the
bowl.  The measured hand position above the bowl is used to modulate the sound volume.  This fluid
up-and-down movement is very intuitive and replaces the circular movement of the mallet.  This
enables a new way of interacting and playing with this traditional instrument.


Finally, the ability to wirelessly network multiple bowls during a performance enables the artist to
spread bowls across an audience and control them all via a central location instead of being
restricted to the arm's length mallet reach, giving the spectators a more visceral experience of
lying down between bowls during a sound bath performance.  Add some super cool LED lighting effects
such as the candle flicker and you have an engaging audio-visual performance!

[A Musical Mushroom automated singing bowl controller installed in a crystal singing bowl.]

How Does it Work?

In local interaction mode, an invisible infrared light beam is emitted vertically above the unit to
measure the distance from the Musical Mushroom's® top surface to a hand hovering above the bowl. 
The presence of a hand will cause the bowl to vibrate constantly at its resonant frequency for as
long as the hand is present.

How Does it Work?

In local interaction mode, an invisible infrared light beam is emitted vertically above the unit to
measure the distance from the Musical Mushroom's® top surface to a hand hovering above the bowl. 
The presence of a hand will cause the bowl to vibrate constantly at its resonant frequency for as
long as the hand is present.  The closer the hand is to the bowl, the louder the sound.  Moving the
hand up and down causes a pleasing tremolo effect, modulating the amplitude similar to the effect
produced by a traditional mallet moving around the rim of the bowl.


In addition, the Musical Mushroom® will automatically detect the hand movement pattern, whether
waving or in a fixed position and will continue it indefinitely when the hand is removed.  This is
useful for generating an automatic drone note effect, enabling the performer to move to playing
other bowls without needing to constantly keep the bowl resonating.  To stop the bowl, the hand is
simply waved in and out of the beam quickly.

How Do I Use It?

There are many creative ways to use the Musical Mushrooms® in a performance.  Whether they are used
to simply drive one or two automatic drone notes in the background to accompany you while you play
your key bowls manually.  You can automate all your bowls and play them using your hands.  You can
connect two Musical Mushrooms® to a single bowl to independently control the main frequency as well
as the overtone (two tones in one bowl).  You can control your bowls while sitting or standing.  You
can distribute your bowls across your audience and travel between them while playing other
instruments.  The sky's the limit!  We are excited to see what creative uses our users will come up
with!! 

## New Possibilities

We are incredibly excited to see where sound practitioners and healers will take this new technology
enabling innovative ways to incorporate sound healing and performance into their practice! 


We also hope to bring vibrational sound instruments to a new generation of users.

frequencies under the guidance of the performer, whether in close proximity using hand gestures or
via wired (USB) control using the MIDI protocol.  One of the many benefits of replacing the mallet
includes the ability to physically extend the performer's range, as well as to automatically hold a
drone note while the performer is free to simultaneously play other bowls or instruments.

[Illustration of how the Musical Mushroom works in a crystal singing bowl]

A novel hand gesture sensor enables local interactions using the performer's hands hovering over the
bowl.  The measured hand position above the bowl is used to modulate the sound volume.  This fluid
up-and-down movement is very intuitive and replaces the circular movement of the mallet.  This
enables a new way of interacting and playing with this traditional instrument.


Finally, the ability to wirelessly network multiple bowls during a performance enables the artist to
spread bowls across an audience and control them all via a central location instead of being
restricted to the arm's length mallet reach, giving the spectators a more visceral experience of
lying down between bowls during a sound bath performance.  Add some super cool LED lighting effects
such as the candle flicker and you have an engaging audio-visual performance!

[A Musical Mushroom automated singing bowl controller installed in a crystal singing bowl.]

How Does it Work?

In local interaction mode, an invisible infrared light beam is emitted vertically above the unit to
measure the distance from the Musical Mushroom's® top surface to a hand hovering above the bowl. 
The presence of a hand will cause the bowl to vibrate constantly at its resonant frequency for as
long as the hand is present.  The closer the hand is to the bowl, the louder the sound.  Moving the
hand up and down causes a pleasing tremolo effect, modulating the amplitude similar to the effect
produced by a traditional mallet moving around the rim of the bowl.


In addition, the Musical Mushroom® will automatically detect the hand movement pattern, whether
waving or in a fixed position and will continue it indefinitely when the hand is removed.  This is
useful for generating an automatic drone note effect, enabling the performer to move to playing
other bowls without needing to constantly keep the bowl resonating.  To stop the bowl, the hand is
simply waved in and out of the beam quickly.

How Do I Use It?

There are many creative ways to use the Musical Mushrooms® in a performance.  Whether they are used
to simply drive one or two automatic drone notes in the background to accompany you while you play
your key bowls manually.  You can automate all your bowls and play them using your hands.  You can
connect two Musical Mushrooms® to a single bowl to independently control the main frequency as well
as the overtone (two tones in one bowl).  You can control your bowls while sitting or standing.  You
can distribute your bowls across your audience and travel between them while playing other
instruments.  The sky's the limit!  We are excited to see what creative uses our users will come up
with!! 

## New Possibilities

We are incredibly excited to see where sound practitioners and healers will take this new technology
enabling innovative ways to incorporate sound healing and performance into their practice! 


We also hope to bring vibrational sound instruments to a new generation of users.

[Musical Mushroom automated singing bowl controllers used in colorful bowls with LED effects during
a live sound bath showing practitioner standing up while playing.]

# Making sure you're not a bot!

Loading...

You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up Anubis to protect the
server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites. This can and does cause
downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.

Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a Proof-of-Work scheme in the vein of Hashcash, a proposed
proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional
load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.

Ultimately, this is a placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and
identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of
work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.

Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

Sadly, you must enable JavaScript to get past this challenge. This is required because AI companies
have changed the social contract around how website hosting works. A no-JS solution is a
work-in-progress.

Protected by [BotStopper][1] From [Techaro][2]. Made with ❤️ in 🇨🇦.

[1]: https://anubis.techaro.lol/docs/admin/botstopper
[2]: https://techaro.lol

MycoStories combines deep sector intelligence with a global expert consulting network to help
founders, investors, and corporates make better decisions, faster - across functional mushrooms,
mycelium materials, mycoprotein, agricultural biologicals, and beyond.

 

Our mission is to accelerate the growth of fungal biotechnology worldwide to address critical
environmental challenges.

# MykoWeb:
# Mushrooms & other Fungi on the Web

Welcome to MykoWeb, WWW pages devoted to the science of mycology (the study of the fungi) and the
hobby of mushrooming (the pursuit of mushrooms). It is a production of [Michael Wood][19], a past
president of the [Mycological Society of San Francisco][20]. MykoWeb was started in the fall of 1995
and was one of the first internet mycology mushrooming sites.

## The Fungi of California

The main attraction at MykoWeb is [The Fungi of California][21], an expanded version of the former
"Fungi of the San Francisco Bay Area". [The Fungi of California][22] contains photographs over
**850** species of mushrooms and other fungi found in California, with over **790** of the species
with descriptions. There are currently over **9700** total photographs of the mushrooms. Included
are links to other online descriptions and photos of the species treated plus references to common
field guides. Also included is a [Glossary][23] of mycological terms and a [Bibliography][24] of
useful mycological references. [The Fungi of California][25] is a joint project of Michael Wood and
Fred Stevens.

## Reprinted Books

MykoWeb has republished four books that are mycological treasures, but long out of print in book
form. The first appears here as [The Boletes of California.][26] This is an online reprint of
*California Mushrooms: A Field Guide to the Boletes* by Dr. Harry D. Thiers. Here you will find keys
and descriptions of the 85 species and varieties of Bolete mushrooms known from California when the
book was published in 1975. [The Boletes of California][27] was done with the permission of Dr.
Harry Thiers and the assistance of Fred Stevens and Michael Boom.

"The book is excellent. Thiers is a top-notch writer. More botanists should write for both the
professional and amateur."
(Clark Rogerson, Managing Editor of *Mycologia*, 1975)

MykoWeb has started a series of mushroom monograph reprints. The first, *[The North American Species
of Pholiota][28]*, is now complete. Included are descriptions of 216 taxa of *Pholiota (sensu
lato)*, with illustrations and photographs. Just completed is the [*North American Species of
Crepidotus* ][29]with descriptions, illustrations, and photographs of 139 taxa.

MykoWeb has also republished the fine mushroom cookbook by Louise Freedman: [Wild About Mushrooms:
the Cookbook of the Mycological Society of San Francisco.][30] The book covers the preparation and
preservation of many wild and cultivated mushroom species. Enjoy the abundance of excellent recipes!

## Photos

MykoWeb is a site rich in mushroom photography. There over 10,800 fungal photographs to view, with
over 9600 of these illustrating the species at [The Fungi of California][31]. Hundreds of the best
photographs are available for viewing in large size on the [Mushroom Photography ][32]pages.

## Much, Much More

Michael Wood is also the creator and former WebMaster of the [Mycological Society of San
Francisco][33] website and served as WebMaster of the North American Mycological Association website
for over four years. Included at MykoWeb is a list of all the amateur [mushroom clubs][34] in North
America, with mailing addresses, web site information, and email contacts.

A mycoblitz is a quick, intense survey of the mushroom and other fungal species present. At the [Pt.
Reyes MycoBlitz][35] pages you can learn about the study of that area that is in progress.
Eventually there will be photos and collection information on all the [voucher specimens][36]
collected in the study.

Other parts of MykoWeb include a page of [Wild Mushroom Recipes][37]. On the [Mushroom Articles][38]
page you will find some fine writing by Steve Trudell (mycorrhiza & book reviews), Mike Boom (fungal
lust!) and Terri Beausejour (cultivation) and many others. Finally there is the [Miscellanea][39]
page. There you can find what does not fit elsewhere, including watercolors, quotes and plates from
old mushroom books, mushroom humor, and several bibliographies, including a copy of my [Bibliography
of the Hypogeous and Secotioid Fungi][40].

The photographs throughout MykoWeb are copyrighted by the photographers who took them and are used
here with their permission. For more information, see [**Use of Photographs at MykoWeb**][41]

Many thanks to all who have helped with these pages. Very special thanks to Fred Stevens, Mike Boom,
and [Taylor F. Lockwood][42].

Thank you for visiting MykoWeb.

# MykoWeb:
# Mushrooms & other Fungi on the Web

Welcome to MykoWeb, WWW pages devoted to the science of mycology (the study of the fungi) and the
hobby of mushrooming (the pursuit of mushrooms). It is a production of [Michael Wood][19], a past
president of the [Mycological Society of San Francisco][20]. MykoWeb was started in the fall of 1995
and was one of the first internet mycology mushrooming sites.

## The Fungi of California

The main attraction at MykoWeb is [The Fungi of California][21], an expanded version of the former
"Fungi of the San Francisco Bay Area". [The Fungi of California][22] contains photographs over
**850** species of mushrooms and other fungi found in California, with over **790** of the species
with descriptions. There are currently over **9700** total photographs of the mushrooms. Included
are links to other online descriptions and photos of the species treated plus references to common
field guides. Also included is a [Glossary][23] of mycological terms and a [Bibliography][24] of
useful mycological references. [The Fungi of California][25] is a joint project of Michael Wood and
Fred Stevens.

## Reprinted Books

MykoWeb has republished four books that are mycological treasures, but long out of print in book
form. The first appears here as [The Boletes of California.][26] This is an online reprint of
*California Mushrooms: A Field Guide to the Boletes* by Dr. Harry D. Thiers. Here you will find keys
and descriptions of the 85 species and varieties of Bolete mushrooms known from California when the
book was published in 1975. [The Boletes of California][27] was done with the permission of Dr.
Harry Thiers and the assistance of Fred Stevens and Michael Boom.

"The book is excellent. Thiers is a top-notch writer. More botanists should write for both the
professional and amateur."
(Clark Rogerson, Managing Editor of *Mycologia*, 1975)

MykoWeb has started a series of mushroom monograph reprints. The first, *[The North American Species
of Pholiota][28]*, is now complete. Included are descriptions of 216 taxa of *Pholiota (sensu
lato)*, with illustrations and photographs. Just completed is the [*North American Species of
Crepidotus* ][29]with descriptions, illustrations, and photographs of 139 taxa.

MykoWeb has also republished the fine mushroom cookbook by Louise Freedman: [Wild About Mushrooms:
the Cookbook of the Mycological Society of San Francisco.][30] The book covers the preparation and
preservation of many wild and cultivated mushroom species. Enjoy the abundance of excellent recipes!

## A review on how Aloha Medicinals was able to organically cultivate the most potent Cordyceps in
## the world that is not only bio-identical genetically, but also bio-identical in it’s analytical
## signature.

Cordyceps has been used for a long time in China and Tibet. For at least a thousand years according
to the written record. It was not until 1972 that the first successful Cordyceps cultivation was
achieved. The first Cordyceps cultures were isolated by the Chinese Academy of Sciences in that
year. These strains were not isolated from Tibet, where most of the top quality Cordyceps comes
from, but rather they were isolated from specimens found in Qinghai province in Central China.
Originally three different strains of Cordyceps were isolated. The first three strains, named CS-1,
CS-2 and CS-3, did not have the fast growth characteristics that make commercial cultivation
practical. It was the fourth culture that had been isolated by this institute, named CS-4, that was
hardy and fast growing. So this CS-4 strain was chosen for commercial production.
This CS-4 culture proved itself a good candidate for commercial growth, so it was evaluated as a
substitute for wild Cordyceps. It was tested for its medical potential, and by 1988 it had been
approved in China as a medicine under the name Jin Shui Bao. As part of the approval process to
bring this to market, many clinical and safety trials were conducted showing its efficacy and
safety. That is the reason there are so many scientific articles available on this particular strain
called CS-4.

But that happened a long time ago in terms of science. Think of the advances that have been made in
all the sciences over the last 44 years. That is how long ago CS-4 was isolated. CS-4 is a good
dietary supplement, but just because CS-4 was the first Cordyceps cultivated and studied certainly
does not mean it is still the best choice today, yet many people today are taken in by the marketers
that still use that early information on CS-4, telling their customers that CS-4 is the best
Cordyceps for their use. This is just simply incorrect. Back in 1972 when CS-4 was isolated there
was no such thing as DNA analysis. So at that time it was not realized that CS-4 contained only a
part of the Cordyceps genome. CS-4 is closely related to Cordyceps sinensis, but it is not “true
Cordyceps sinensis”. CS-4 is a related species called an Anamorph.

Let’s jump ahead nearly 40 years and look at where Cordyceps cultivation is today: Aloha Medicinals
set out to cultivate the most potent Cordyceps back in 1999. Aloha started with the purchase of CS-4
cultures from private manufacturers in China. This was the first strain of Cordyceps Aloha produced
when the company was formed on Maui in 2000. In 2001 Aloha purchased another ten Cordyceps strains
from the Government of China. But Alohas research using DNA analysis and the most up-to-date
analytical methods such as GC/MS and HPLC/MS showed that none of these “Cordyceps” strains were
identical to wild Cordyceps. They were all related anamorphs, but they were not “True Cordyceps”.

Aloha tried every possible combination of culture techniques and growth medium, but realized that by
using these part-spore cultures there was no way to gain the full potential which is known to occur
in wild Cordyceps. To achieve the wild Cordyceps quality requires a much more complex approach,
involving the replication of the wild Cordyceps growth conditions and triggering fusion between
several part-spore cultures to achieve the full Cordyceps DNA sequence. This approach was so unique
it was issued the only patent ever granted for the hybridization of mushrooms! **This is the only
cultivated Cordyceps available today that is genetically and analytically Bio-Identical to the wild
Cordyceps occurring in Nature.** This is not to be confused with Genetic Modification. Aloha
Medicinals absolutely guarantees there are NO genetically modified organisms (GMO) in any Aloha
Medicinals product. Aloha is opposed to the GMO approach, as well as this being forbidden under USDA
and EU Certified Organic standards. Quality has no substitute. **Aloha Medicinals makes the VERY
BEST medicinal mushroom products in the world today**

Even after Aloha had developed these bio-identical cultures though, which were 100% Cordyceps
sinensis in every way, there was still a problem: The Cordyceps being grown in cultivation was still
not as potent as the wild collected Cordyceps. To try and resolve this problem, **Aloha Medicinals
scientists undertook an expedition into the heartland of wild Cordyceps habitat, central Tibet.** In
May and June of 2006 Aloha Medicinals conducted one of the most comprehensive scientific research
expeditions ever undertaken in the mountains of Tibet to study the natural growth parameters of wild
Cordyceps. Working with the local nomad people, Aloha identified several hundred Cordyceps specimens
growing directly from the ground. Aloha carefully measured all the growth conditions there, such as
pH, soil and air temperature and composition, moisture content in the air and soil, the other
micro-organisms found in the area, air pressure and virtually everything else that could be
measured, Aloha did.

Aloha brought this information back to the lab, and developed entirely new methods of cultivation,
which have resulted in Cordyceps that is not only bio-identical genetically, but also bio-identical
in it’s analytical signature. Bringing the latest of 21st century American biotechnology to this
field has resulted in a quantum leap in Cordyceps cultivation, reducing the cost and increasing the
quality of cultivated Cordyceps. **These cultivation methods involved building special growing
chambers where the oxygen is held at 50% of the normal atmospheric oxygen, and the temperature is
held at just above freezing. This exactly replicates the conditions found during the growing season
in Nepal and Tibet at 18,000 feet (5400 meters) elevation. This Low Temperature, Low Oxygen growth
is also patented. Aloha Medicinals is the only company in the world that grows Cordyceps using these
techniques.**
